findings.evidence: Proof body: `filter_upwards [...] with w h1 h2 h3; exact (h1.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.mul (h3.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.comp w h2.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt)).deriv`. Only differentiability is used.
findings.fix: State it as `(hp : ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 z, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 p w) (hφ : ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 z, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 φ w) (hF : ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 z, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 F (φ w))` without `CompleteSpace`. If convenient, keep a short `AnalyticAt` corollary derived from it.
findings.issue: `deriv_mul_comp_eventuallyEq` requires `AnalyticAt` for `p`, `φ`, `F` and `[CompleteSpace 𝕜]`, but the proof uses only `differentiableAt` at nearby points (`h1.differentiableAt`, `h2.differentiableAt`, `h3.differentiableAt`). Over ℝ this excludes non-analytic smooth data, and it falls short of Mathlib's convention of differentiability hypotheses in deriv calculus.

findings.evidence: Proof uses `hF.deriv.differentiableAt`, `hp.deriv.differentiableAt`, `hφ.deriv.differentiableAt`, `hF.differentiableAt`, `hφ.differentiableAt`, `hp.differentiableAt`. These are pointwise differentiability facts, which analyticity is used only to supply.
findings.fix: Derive it from the generalized first lemma under the hypotheses `DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (deriv p) z`, `DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (deriv φ) z`, `DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (deriv F) (φ z)`, plus the eventual differentiability. Keep the analytic form, if wanted, as a one-line corollary.
findings.issue: `deriv_deriv_mul_comp` needs only the eventual differentiability above plus differentiability of `deriv p`, `deriv φ` at `z` and of `deriv F` at `φ z`. Requiring analyticity limits a generic-field second-order product and chain rule to analytic data.

summary: The main theorem is the pinned roadmap statement, so its unused `hβγ`/`hU` hypotheses are acceptable. The new public helpers in `TauCeti/Analysis/Analytic/Deriv.lean` are stated over a general field but require `AnalyticAt` and `CompleteSpace`, while their proofs need only differentiability.
